title: Prescription Insurance on File Corrected Claim Patient Pay
content:
## Rate definition

Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, the corrected claim is made for the most recent reversal on the coverage made for a billing correction. The fill a corrected claim is for is the refill of the prescription the reversed claim billed that carries the fill number the reversed claim billed.

The patient pay of a corrected claim is the plan's standard copay, **25.00**, for each **30** days of the corrected fill's supply, prorated per day, and rounded to the cent once, as the last operation.

## In other words

- The per-day charge is 25.00 divided by 30.
- The charge is that per-day figure multiplied by the corrected fill's days supply.
- Only the final amount is rounded to the cent.

## Worked figures (hypothetical fills)

| Corrected fill's days supply | 25.00 multiplied by the days supply, divided by 30 | Patient pay |
|---|---|---|
| 30 | 25.00 | 25.00 |
| 20 | 16.6666… | 16.67 |
| 45 | 37.50 | 37.50 |
| 90 | 75.00 | 75.00 |
| 7 | 5.8333… | 5.83 |

## Identifying the fill (hypothetical records)

The coverage shows two reversals made for a billing correction, on 2 May and on 9 May. The corrected claim is made for the 9 May reversal. That reversal cancelled a claim for prescription A, fill number 3; the fill the corrected claim is for is refill number 3 of prescription A, and its days supply is the days supply that refill dispensed.
